subject: DPA & KMS model for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments — scope and subprocessors
content:
From: Lori Pierce <lori.pierce@photonhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@photonhealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA & KMS for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and infosec teams reviewed Redwood's private deployment options and have a few open items before we can sign the DPA: 1) explicit subprocessors list for the on-prem package (we need to enumerate any managed services Redwood will call out to, even in VPC), 2) confirmation that Photon controls the KMS keys (we prefer customer-managed keys with BYOK and no Redwood access), 3) cross-border transfer language — our data residency requirements are US-only and we need contractual guarantees around personnel and backups, and 4) support access model (breakglass process, audit trail, and scope of remote debugging).

Can you point us to the latest redlines and subprocessors inventory? We're on a tight timeline for our July 1 pilot.

Thanks,
Lori Pierce
Head of Legal — Photon Health

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA & KMS for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments

Hi Lori — appreciate the clear list. Attaching our current DPA draft with inline notes and a CSV of our current subprocessors for private deployments. Quick summary on the asks:

- Subprocessors: the on-prem/VPC package is largely customer-controlled, but there are a small set of Redwood-managed components we may use for telemetry aggregation and optional marketplace integrations. These are listed in the attached CSV. We can contractually commit to a notification window (30 days) for changes and allow you the right to object.

- KMS/BYOK: We support customer-controlled keys for both VPC and air-gapped on-prem installs. The standard model is that Photon supplies an externally managed HSM/KMS endpoint (or we accept a wrapped key) — Redwood has no persistent plaintext access to the root keys. I'll loop in Neha and Rishi from Security/Legal to confirm the exact wording we can commit to.

- Cross-border & backups: For hosted artifacts that Redwood controls (e.g., license entitlements, telemetry), we can commit to US-only storage for your account and to contractually prohibit staff in high-risk regions from accessing PH data. For full on-prem installs, customer data stays in your environment — our SLA language still allows limited diagnostic packages to be collected if you opt-in.

- Support access: we have a breakglass playbook (attached) that requires an authorized Photon contact + signed release and results in a time-bound ephemeral session with audit logging.

I'll get formal redlines from Legal today.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed_DPA_PH_redlines.docx, subprocessors_list_2026-08-19.csv, support-breakglass-playbook.pdf

Thanks for the initial response, Jonas. Quick technical clarifications from our side to put into the DPA:

- KMS flow: for VPC deployments we support an external Cloud KMS (customer project), and for on-prem we support KMIP/HSM endpoints. In all cases photons' keys are used to encrypt model state and any persisted KV caches. Redwood holds no master key. We can include diagrams (see attached) for the SRE/Infra review.

- Subprocessors CSV: note that the CSV lists (A) telemetry collector (option, off by default), (B) license entitlements handling (Redwood-hosted control plane), and (C) monitoring/alerting partner for Dedicated support. For strict privacy customers we can offer a bounded scope exclusion for (A) and (C) via contract.

- Personnel and backup access: We propose language that prohibits staff outside the US from accessing PH customer data and requires any remote access be via a logged, time-limited session with an auditable ticket.

Neha — tagging you for legal/KMS exact wording. Rishi — can you confirm whether we can accept a clause that prohibits Redwood from decrypting backups without an emergency legal process?

Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, Lori Pierce <lori.pierce@photonhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA & KMS for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments — proposed legal language

Lori / Photon team —

Attached are the proposed contractual redlines. Key points we're comfortable committing to (summary):

1) Subprocessors & notifications: Redwood will provide an up-to-date subprocessors list and will provide 30 days' notice before onboarding a new subprocessor that will process Photon customer data. Photon will have the right to object in writing and request mitigation; if unresolved, both parties can escalate to senior legal contacts to resolve.

2) KMS / BYOK: We will include a BYOK clause for both VPC and on-prem installs. For VPC, Photon can attach a customer-managed KMS (Cloud provider) with RBAC limiting Redwood's controller role to only key-wrapping operations. For on-prem, we support direct KMIP/HSM endpoints or wrapped-key imports. Contractually, Redwood will not request or store plaintext customer master keys.

3) Breakglass / support: We can agree to a breakglass process that requires (a) Photon authorization, (b) short-lived ephemeral credentials, and (c) comprehensive audit logs that Photon can review. We will also describe the minimal diagnostic artifact set and retain that any data shipped to Redwood for debugging will be purpose-limited and automatically deleted after agreed retention.

4) Cross-border transfers: For Photon, we will add a clause to store all account-linked hosted artifacts within US regions only and to restrict support personnel access accordingly. For encrypted backups that reside in customer infrastructure, Redwood will not hold keys and therefore cannot perform cross-border restoration without Photon action.

5) Emergency access: We cannot create an absolute bar to lawful process (e.g., valid court order). We will add a transparency clause — Redwood will notify Photon of any compelled disclosure where permitted by law and will only disclose the narrow request.

Next steps: 1) Photon legal to review attached redlines and flag any language they find unacceptable, 2) we incorporate final changes and prepare DocuSign, 3) we schedule a final 30-minute call to walk legal/Sec through the breakglass playbook.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed_DPA_PH_redlines.docx

From: Lori Pierce <lori.pierce@photonhealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@novamed.co>, Greenline Legal <legal@greenline.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA & KMS for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments — proposed legal language

Neha / Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough responses and the attachments. A few follow-ups from our counsel: 

- Object window: 30 days is acceptable, but we need a contractual mechanism if Redwood adds a subprocessor that materially increases risk (e.g., a third-party data enrichment or external model evaluation partner). We propose Redwood must either remove PH data from that subprocessor or offer the option to terminate the contract without penalty.

- Backups: We will require a clause that prevents Redwood from restoring customer data into non-US environments even in disaster scenarios unless Photon explicitly requests it.

- Breakglass: we appreciate the playbook — can you confirm that the playbook includes SIEM log exports and SHA-256 checksums of any artifacts sent to Redwood? We need cryptographic integrity and the ability to independently verify what was sent.

We will consolidate our redlines and upload a single marked-up DPA by EOD Monday.

Best,
Lori

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA & KMS for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments — support & backups confirmation

Lori — quick confirmations from infra/security:

- Subprocessor risk: we can add a remediation path as requested: if a new subprocessor creates a material incremental risk and cannot be mitigated, Photon can require Redwood to stop sending new data to that subprocessor or terminate with a 60-day cure period and an option for unilateral termination for material breaches.

- Backup restoration: for hosted artifacts, we will commit to US-only restores. For customer-managed on-prem backups, any restoration into a Redwood-controlled environment requires Photon authorization in writing (DocuSign is fine).

- SIEM & checksums: our breakglass playbook includes SIEM exports and SHA-256 checksums of any diagnostic bundles. We'll add explicit language to the DPA referencing the audit artifacts and retention period.

If Photon is comfortable with these additions we'll finalize the doc and circulate DocuSign links.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
